truthBoundary: This catalog is a textbook placement map. A listed source, upstream Lean cluster, or extended chapter is not a local ASPBE theorem unless an exact compiled declaration is linked separately.

parts.label: Part I
parts.title: State Preparation
parts.summary: The compiled preparation contract and finite examples are joined by source-audited routes for structured, scalable state loading.

chapters.title: Compiled preparation contracts and certificates
chapters.summary: Normalized targets, unitary candidates, first-column semantics and exact finite witnesses.

chapters.title: Walsh-series state preparation
chapters.summary: Walsh phase synthesis, controlled constant mode, interference, postselection, infidelity and successful-preparation cost.

chapters.title: Diagonal filters as state-preparation suppliers
chapters.summary: Apply a unitary or dilated non-unitary diagonal to a charged input, then account for normalization, success and finite precision.

parts.label: Part II
parts.title: Block Encoding
parts.summary: The compiled clean-block API and construction rules are extended by source-faithful diagonal, compiler and resource routes.

chapters.title: Compiled block contracts and composition rules
chapters.summary: Clean-block extraction, LCU/product routes, sparse access, resource records and finite certified cases.

chapters.title: Unitary and non-unitary diagonal operators
chapters.summary: Separate phase operators from dilated filters and prove matched space–time–accuracy contracts, including cleanup and error-scale adapters.

chapters.title: Fourier and structured linear-operator suppliers
chapters.summary: Connect exact Fourier circuit resources and structured operator descriptions to the shared circuit and block interfaces without treating either as an automatic block encoding.

parts.label: Part III
parts.title: Quantum Information and Representation Theory
parts.summary: Leditzky's representation-theoretic QIT notes organize one shared state/channel foundation followed by symmetry, Schur–Weyl and information-theoretic applications.

chapters.title: States, density operators and measurements
chapters.summary: Choose one canonical finite-dimensional state, positive-operator, Born-rule and POVM layer before importing downstream results.

chapters.title: Composite systems, partial trace and purification
chapters.summary: Freeze subsystem order and tensor conventions; purification and dilation remain non-unique representative constructions.

chapters.title: Channels, Choi maps, distances and operational tests
chapters.summary: Completely positive maps, Kraus/Choi representations, trace/fidelity conventions and contractivity become shared nodes.

chapters.title: Finite-group and unitary representation foundations
chapters.summary: Group actions, representations, characters, averaging and fixed spaces are admitted only after manuscript-specific namespaces are purified.

chapters.title: Young diagrams, Specht modules and Schur–Weyl duality
chapters.summary: Build the symmetric-group/unitary-group bridge needed by the quantum method of types; advanced Saxl and Foulkes–Howe results remain extensions, not prerequisites.

chapters.title: Invariant states, de Finetti, cloning and spectrum estimation
chapters.summary: Consume the shared QIT and representation layers without turning conceptual symmetry correspondences into Lean dependencies.

chapters.title: Capacity, entanglement, secret key and games
chapters.summary: Amplitude-damping capacity, entangled games and dimension-ten zero-key constructions are source routes above canonical state/channel adapters.

chapters.title: Extended chapter: quantum optics and channel counterexamples
chapters.summary: Photon-number entropy, PPT-square phenomena and explicit channel geometry are advanced consumers, not foundational definitions.

parts.label: Part IV
parts.title: Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation
parts.summary: Lin–Wiebe's scientific-computing progression reuses Part II Block Encoding and adds transforms, simulation, estimation and application contracts.

chapters.title: Probability, channels, query models, perturbation and statistics
chapters.summary: Share QIT states/channels/distances and make query construction, precision and readout costs explicit.

chapters.title: Block encoding as the shared scientific-computing interface
chapters.summary: Point back to Part II and add adapters only where the source notation or error convention differs.

chapters.title: Amplification, qubitization, QSP and QSVT
chapters.summary: Separate polynomial/signal-transform correctness from phase synthesis and finite-gate compilation.

chapters.title: Hamiltonian simulation and dynamics
chapters.summary: Compose access, block/qubitization suppliers, approximation and successful execution under one resource tier.

chapters.title: Fourier transforms, phase estimation and amplitude estimation
chapters.summary: Use the Comparator-backed exact Fourier route as an external resource theorem after circuit-model adaptation; it does not itself certify QPE.

chapters.title: Eigenvalue and ground-state algorithms
chapters.summary: Charge trial-state preparation, overlap, gap, precision, amplification and final classical output.

chapters.title: Linear systems, differential equations and open systems
chapters.summary: Reuse block/channel nodes and expose input, condition-number, success and readout assumptions rather than hiding them in an oracle.

chapters.title: Extended chapter: compilers, synthesis and circuit lower bounds
chapters.summary: Exact factoring, shallow-circuit parity and oracle-assisted unitary synthesis extend the computing curriculum without counting as SP/BE successes.

chapters.title: Extended chapter: many-body model targets
chapters.summary: The Comparator-backed Laughlin route is a model-side spectral target and reusable mathematical substrate, not evidence of a quantum algorithm or simulator.
